title: 207 - Faxanadu
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Faxanadu
items.description: The episode's game, a side-scrolling action RPG set on a giant world tree, whose title the hosts debate how to pronounce.

items.name: Xanadu
items.description: The earlier Dragon Slayer action RPG that Faxanadu is a spinoff of; the name is a blend of Famicom and Xanadu.

items.name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
items.description: The side-scrolling action RPG that Faxanadu is constantly compared to, with an overworld map the hosts debate.

links.label: Wikipedia: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link

items.episode_title: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link

items.name: Metroid
items.description: Used as an example of a game with interconnected areas but no overworld map.

items.name: Yggdrasil
items.description: The world tree idea behind the game's setting, a common trope in Japanese games and stories.

links.label: Wikipedia: World tree
links.note: Motif in many mythologies and religions

items.name: The Legend of Zelda
items.description: Its shield logo and manual presentation are compared to how Faxanadu's box art sells a grand quest.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda (video game)

items.name: Dragon Warrior
items.description: The previous week's turn-based RPG, used as a contrast for experience, gold, shops and saving.

items.name: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest
items.description: Another NES action RPG hybrid, mentioned for cryptic text and towns.

items.name: Dragon Slayer
items.description: The Falcom RPG series that Faxanadu's predecessor belongs to.

items.name: Bloodborne
items.description: Its opening, where a beast kills you before you have a weapon, is compared to the first town.

items.name: Dragon Quest XI
items.description: A recent game with a world tree, cited as an example of the trope.

items.name: Xenoblade Chronicles 2
items.description: Another recent game with a giant tree, cited as an example of the trope.

items.name: Final Fantasy IX
items.description: Another game that features a world tree.

items.name: ROM hacking
items.description: Fan modifications of old games, suggested as a way to fix balance problems and bugs.

items.name: Final Fantasy
items.description: The original game, cited with Dragon Warrior as having ROM hacks that rebalance experience points.

items.name: RPG Maker
items.description: The game-creation software that a Charles Barkley NES-era game is guessed to have been made with.

links.label: Wikipedia: RPG Maker
links.note: Video game creation system software series

items.name: Barkley, Shut Up and Jam!
items.description: The hosts wonder whether this basketball RPG was a ROM hack or a real game.

links.label: Wikipedia: Barkley Shut Up and Jam!

items.name: Bill Murray
items.description: The hosts joke that the smoking shopkeeper looks like him.

items.name: Xanadu Next
items.description: A later Xanadu game that first came out on the N-Gage in 2005, then on PC.

items.name: N-Gage
items.description: Nokia's phone and handheld game console, where Xanadu Next first appeared.

links.label: Wikipedia: N-Gage
links.note: Mobile phone and handheld game system

items.name: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
items.description: The one N-Gage game one host remembers, from TV ads showing the vertical screen.

items.name: Lost
items.description: The TV show that one host was watching when the N-Gage ads aired.

items.name: Tales of
items.description: The JRPG series cited as a trend Xanadu Next followed.

items.name: Tokyo Xanadu
items.description: A Persona-like action RPG built from Xanadu Next's gameplay, on PS Vita and PS4.

items.name: Persona
items.description: The Atlus RPG series the hosts compare Tokyo Xanadu to.

items.name: Legacy of the Wizard
items.description: The NES version of Dragon Slayer IV, where you play a family in a huge underground cave with heavy backtracking.

items.name: The Witcher
items.description: Used as an example of a modern game one host gets absorbed in, like Faxanadu.

items.name: Flying Dragon: The Secret Scroll
items.description: The next episode's game, another dragon-themed title.

links.label: Wikipedia: Flying Dragon: The Secret Scroll

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: The show's running list of must-play NES games, which this game joins.
